extracted.intended_audience: Johns Hopkins University communications staff, press officers, and writers preparing JHU press releases and news content
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating Johns Hopkins University press releases and news communications that follow institution-specific style, newsworthiness criteria, and media-relations practices. Emphasizes AP style, clear/accessible academic tone, and what the university considers newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical structure (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JHU-quality press releases should have strong organization; use the inverted pyramid structure so the most important information appears first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling argument (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a persuasive case for why the item matters to readers and journalists; emphasize relevance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Easy to understand (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon; write plainly so academic content is accessible to a general audience while remaining accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Single main message (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A release should have one clear central message or news peg and avoid diluting it with multiple unrelated points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth transitions (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure logical progression between paragraphs and sentences so the reader can follow the argument or narrative easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate to audience and purpose (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an academic but accessible tone—professional and authoritative while understandable to journalists and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar and word choice (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe correct grammar, syntax, and precise word choice consistent with AP style and Hopkins conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Current and relevant (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release topics should be timely for news cycles and aligned with events, discoveries, awards, or other immediate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifiable facts (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All factual claims must be checkable; include clear attribution, sources, and verifiable data to support assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters to readers (one of the 10 Tenets of Good Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize why the story matters beyond the university—its impact on policy, community, science, or public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the most important information at the top (explicit in the implicit rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the key news; follow with supporting details, context, quotes, and then background information.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Associated Press style for punctuation, capitalization, numbers, and general style conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP style is the default for JHU editorial content; consult the AP Stylebook for specifics and resolve conflicts with Chicago only when noted by Hopkins guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hopkins-specific terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Johns Hopkins–preferred institutional terms and naming conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency with Hopkins internal terminology lists to avoid conflicting or informal names for schools, centers, and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling of institutional name
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Johns Hopkins' (never 'John Hopkins').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use the correct, full institutional name; double-check in headlines and lead sentences where errors are most visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct school names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use official school names such as 'Bloomberg School of Public Health' exactly as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing specific schools, use the official, full names to ensure accuracy and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty titles consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Present faculty titles consistently (e.g., associate professor, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized title forms per Hopkins guidance; do not embellish or create unofficial titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departments capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize department names per Hopkins style guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the style guide's capitalization rules for departments and units to maintain institutional consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media-relations proactive outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect with journalists, reach out regularly with news releases, send advisories, and provide story ideas (Media Relations Approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain relationships with reporters, adopt regular outreach schedules, use advisories for embargoed items, and pitch story ideas beyond formal releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant research findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify major research discoveries as newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novel, impactful research with clear implications and accessible explanations for non-specialist audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major awards and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat major awards/honors received by faculty or the institution as newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame awards in terms of significance, prestige, and what they mean for the institution or field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider substantial research grants as newsworthy items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the grant's purpose, scale, funding source, and anticipated impact or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable hires
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on high-profile faculty/staff hires as newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about the hire's expertise, role, and expected contributions to the university and field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicize innovations (technology, methods, programs) that represent advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what is new, why it matters, potential applications, and any commercialization or partnership context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize news with implications for public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how findings or events could influence policy decisions, public debate, or regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight work that affects local or broader communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate tangible community outcomes, partnerships, or benefits resulting from university activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases should be persuasive on relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinforce that releases must communicate why the content is relevant to audiences and journalists (implicit rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame facts and quotes to clarify relevance, with a clear news peg and implications for stakeholders.
